title: macOS Performance Issue
scenario: Ms. Williams, a drama teacher, calls the IT service desk. Her MacBook Pro (macOS 14.6) has become painfully slow over the past two weeks. Apps take 30-60 seconds to open. Activity Monitor shows the kernel_task process consuming 80%+ CPU continuously. Fans are running at maximum speed. She has a production deadline — the spring musical program needs to be printed and distributed by Friday.
impact: Instructional: Spring musical programs are blocked by the slow Mac. Deadline is Friday. This is a high-urgency instructional impact.
objectives: Identify the root cause of kernel_task CPU spikes and thermal throttling
Collect evidence including Activity Monitor readings and temperature data
Determine whether this is a software or hardware issue
Resolve the issue or escalate appropriately with documentation
Document the troubleshooting steps and resolution

evidence.description: Screenshot of Activity Monitor showing kernel_task at 80%+ CPU
Apple Diagnostics result (reference code if any)
Temperature sensor readings from the MacBook
Result of booting in Safe Mode — does the issue persist?

decisionPoints.prompt: Ms. Williams' MacBook shows kernel_task consuming 80%+ CPU with thermal throttling. What is the most likely root cause?

options.label: Hardware thermal issue — elevated ambient temperature or degraded thermal paste causing the CPU to throttle
options.feedback: Correct. kernel_task consuming high CPU with thermal throttling is the hallmark of a hardware thermal management issue. The system is throttling itself to prevent damage.

options.label: A problematic kernel extension (kext) is driving CPU spikes and must be unloaded
options.feedback: A rogue kext could cause elevated CPU, but the sustained thermal throttling pattern is more consistent with heat management. A kext issue would not typically cause thermal throttling without an underlying heat source.

options.label: Malware on the MacBook is generating the CPU load and must be scanned and removed
options.feedback: macOS malware is rare and would not present as kernel_task thermal throttling. This diagnosis lacks evidence and leads to the wrong remediation path.

decisionPoints.prompt: To isolate whether this is a hardware thermal failure or a software-triggered heat issue, what should you do first?

options.label: Boot in Safe Mode to rule out third-party software as a contributing factor
options.feedback: Good thinking. Safe Mode isolates the software environment. If kernel_task is still throttling in Safe Mode, the issue is hardware thermal. If it resolves, software is contributing.

options.label: Run Apple Diagnostics immediately to check for hardware sensor failures
options.feedback: Correct. Apple Diagnostics will check thermal sensors and fans directly. If sensors are failing, this will show a reference code. This is the most direct hardware test.

options.label: Reset the SMC to clear thermal management state and restart the system
options.feedback: Resetting the SMC is a valid step, but it should follow evidence collection. You cannot diagnose whether hardware is failing if you immediately reset and restart.

ticket.initialDescription: MacBook Pro (macOS 14.6) painfully slow — kernel_task at 80%+ CPU, fans at max, apps taking 30-60 seconds. Deadline Friday for spring musical programs.

nodes.title: Intake
nodes.body: Ms. Williams calls. Her MacBook Pro has been painfully slow for two weeks. kernel_task is at 80%+ CPU, fans are maxed, apps take 30-60 seconds. She has a Friday deadline for spring musical programs. Acknowledge the urgency, take notes, and open a ticket.

nodes.title: Inspect Activity Monitor and system state
nodes.body: Review the MacBook's Activity Monitor snapshot. Note kernel_task CPU usage, RAM pressure, and thermal state. Document the exact readings as evidence. Ask Ms. Williams what changed two weeks ago — new software, location, or behavior?

nodes.title: Identify the root cause
nodes.body: kernel_task is at 82% CPU with thermal throttling and fans at 6200 RPM. Based on the evidence and the pattern of symptoms, identify the most likely root cause.

nodes.title: Choose the next diagnostic step
nodes.body: Before committing to a resolution, choose the most appropriate next step to confirm whether this is hardware or software.

nodes.title: Apply resolution or escalate
nodes.body: Based on the diagnostic results: if Apple Diagnostics shows a hardware reference code, this requires escalation to Apple Store / authorized repair with a hardware ticket. If Safe Mode resolves it, a software uninstallation or OS reinstall may be needed. Document your findings and next steps.

nodes.title: Validate performance restoration
nodes.body: Confirm that kernel_task CPU has returned to normal (<5%), thermal status is nominal, and fans are at standard RPM. Ask Ms. Williams to test opening two apps to confirm the improvement.

nodes.title: Document the ticket
nodes.body: Write a clear ticket resolution. Include root cause, diagnostic steps taken, resolution applied, and guidance for Ms. Williams if the issue recurs.
nodes.prompt: Write a follow-up message to Ms. Williams. Acknowledge the deadline pressure, explain the root cause in plain language, and confirm the system is ready for Friday's program work.

nodes.title: Debrief
nodes.body: Review your score and reflect on the thermal throttling diagnosis pattern.

kbOpportunity: kernel_task thermal throttling on MacBook Pro — when Activity Monitor shows kernel_task consuming high CPU with thermal throttling, check Apple Diagnostics for hardware sensor failures before assuming a software cause.
